heroHeadline: Day 582: Sheinbaum's Cinco de Mayo Sovereignty Speech in Puebla; Plan México Acciones Launched; FIRA Debt Relief for 46,567 Small Producers; USMCA Round Set for May 25
heroSubtitle: The week of May 3–6, 2026 marked a decisive phase of the Sheinbaum administration's sovereignty assertion and economic response. On May 3, the Morena National Council convened and elected former Social Welfare Secretary Ariadna Montiel Reyes as Morena's new national president, while the FGR continued its review of the U.S. DOJ extradition request for Sinaloa Governor Rocha Moya (finding insufficient evidence). On May 4, Sheinbaum launched 'Plan México Acciones' with Economy Secretary Ebrard — a $298B-pipeline investment acceleration package featuring 41–91% tax deductions on fixed-asset investments, a Presidential Investment Office, and a 30-day authorization window — in direct response to Q1 2026's -0.8% GDP contraction. On May 5, in the most symbolically charged address of the sovereignty crisis, Sheinbaum traveled to Puebla for the Cinco de Mayo military ceremony, swearing in 31,000 soldiers and issuing her sharpest warning yet: 'No foreign power is going to tell Mexicans how to govern ourselves. Those who seek foreign support, as they lack the people's support, are destined for defeat.' On May 6, at the mañanera, Sheinbaum announced cancellation of unpayable FIRA agricultural debts for 46,567 small producers (13,400 women farmers' guarantees released), proposed the next IPN director be chosen via public consultation, confirmed National Guard elements are protecting Rocha Moya during his leave, and confirmed Luisa María Alcalde's integration into the presidential communications team. Approval rating has fallen to ~51% (end-April). The first formal USMCA bilateral negotiating round remains on track for the week of May 25 in Mexico City.
